The Skylab Mission

America's First Space Station

Skylab was the United States' first space station, designed to prove that humans could live and work in space for extended periods. Operating from May 1973 to February 1974, it served as a laboratory for scientific experiments, Earth observations, and solar studies, laying the groundwork for future space stations like the International Space Station.

Launch

May 14, 1973

Launched aboard the last Saturn V rocket

Mass

77,088 kg

Including the Apollo Telescope Mount

Dimensions

36.1m length

Largest object in orbit at the time

Deorbit

July 11, 1979

Fell over Western Australia

Scientific Objectives

Medical Research

Purpose: Study effects of long-duration spaceflight on human physiology

  • Bone density loss and muscle atrophy
  • Cardiovascular deconditioning
  • Space motion sickness adaptation
  • Psychological effects of isolation
Achievement: Established medical protocols for future long-duration missions

Solar Astronomy

Purpose: Observe the Sun without atmospheric interference

  • Solar flare monitoring and prediction
  • Coronal mass ejection studies
  • Solar cycle observation
  • X-ray and ultraviolet solar imaging
Achievement: Over 127,000 solar photographs taken

Earth Observation

Purpose: Study Earth's resources, weather, and environmental changes

  • Agricultural crop monitoring
  • Ocean current mapping
  • Geological surveys
  • Weather pattern analysis
Achievement: 45,000 Earth photographs for resource management

Materials Science

Purpose: Utilize microgravity for materials research

  • Crystal growth experiments
  • Metal alloy formation
  • Protein crystallization
  • Fluid dynamics studies
Achievement: Pioneered space-based manufacturing techniques

Astronomy

Purpose: Observe celestial objects without atmospheric distortion

  • Star formation studies
  • Galaxy mapping
  • Comet Kohoutek observations
  • Deep space photography
Achievement: First comprehensive space-based astronomical survey

Technology Testing

Purpose: Test technologies for future space missions

  • Life support system validation
  • Spacewalk procedures
  • Spacecraft maintenance techniques
  • Long-term equipment reliability
Achievement: Validated technologies used on Space Shuttle and ISS

Historical Impact

Bridge to the Future

Skylab served as the crucial link between the Apollo lunar program and the Space Shuttle era. It demonstrated that the United States could successfully operate long-duration space missions and maintain human presence in orbit.

International Cooperation

The mission laid groundwork for future international partnerships in space, including the Apollo-Soyuz Test Project and eventually the International Space Station program.

Scientific Foundation

Research conducted on Skylab directly contributed to medical countermeasures, life support systems, and operational procedures still used on the International Space Station today.
